limitations: Native requirement mapping is preserved; independent semantic coverage and targeted positive/negative/equivalent game fixtures have not been qualified.

requirements.obligation: The game enters its playable scene.
Natural scene start.

The playable arena uses the supplied board floor and wall meshes together with the complete 10x10 cell and wall arrangement identified as `rollball-fixed-maze-10x10-v2` in the supplied fixed-layout data.
All perimeter and internal walls in that layout are present as gameplay collision boundaries.
The arena must not procedurally regenerate, choose another seed, omit layout walls, add route-changing walls, replace the supplied board meshes, or substitute a different maze.
The full fixed board is visible from the normal play view and the supplied board geometry is recognizable.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: The same layout and supplied board meshes must remain in use after trap recovery, `R` restart, and true process reopen.
`LAYOUT-01` is present.
Natural scene start.
The ball starts at the center of cell `(0,0)`, the exit occupies cell `(9,9)`, and coordinates use the supplied bottom-left origin, with `x` increasing right and `y` increasing up.
The start, exit, or traps must not move, duplicate, disappear, change type, or lose the supplied hole geometry between runs.
Start, trap openings, and exit cells are visually distinguishable.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Trap recovery, restart, and reopen restore exactly these cells and the supplied trap-hole presentation.
The playable scene is active.
Natural scene start and normal movement.
A stable top-down camera shows the entire 10x10 maze at once.
Screen up corresponds to increasing layout `y`, and screen right corresponds to increasing layout `x`.
The ball, walls, traps, and exit remain readable throughout normal play.
The camera must not rotate, mirror the layout, follow so closely that required cells leave the view, or become controlled by mouse movement.
The maze orientation and all gameplay-critical objects remain clear.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Camera orientation and framing remain the same after trap recovery, restart, and reopen.
Status is `RUNNING` and the ball is not in trap recovery.
Hold `W`, `A`, `S`, or `D`, then release it.
`W` drives the ball toward increasing `y`, `S` toward decreasing `y`, `A` toward decreasing `x`, and `D` toward increasing `x`.
Holding a key continues applying motion input; releasing it stops applying that directional input.
Opposite and diagonal key combinations may be handled by any consistent physics implementation.
Input must not teleport the ball, directly set success, disable collisions, or work only through a debug or evaluator-only path.
The ball visibly accelerates in the requested direction when not blocked.

The motion has a deliberately slippery feel: releasing a key removes new drive but does not instantly cancel existing travel, and a direction change needs a short counter-steering interval before the ball settles into the new direction.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Movement input is ignored while the run is completed and while trap recovery has temporarily disabled control.
Status is `RUNNING`.
Apply and release movement input.
The supplied 3D sphere mesh is the visible player object.

It uses continuous physical motion: its world position changes across frames, the sphere visibly rotates around a horizontal axis as it travels, and it retains bounded momentum after input release before damping or collision slows it.
The player can read the ball’s three-dimensional shading and rotation from the normal camera.
The ball must not be replaced by a 2D sprite, flat icon, primitive, unrelated mesh, cell-center teleport, instant route traversal, or visually unrotated sliding marker.
Translation, three-dimensional form, and rolling rotation are all visible from the top-down camera.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Repeated direction changes remain stable and controllable; restart or reset removes old linear and angular velocity.
The ball is moving during `RUNNING`.
Drive the ball with noticeable speed into a perimeter or internal wall.
The wall physically blocks the ball.
On a clear non-zero-speed impact, the ball visibly bounces/rebounds away from the wall by reversing its inward motion, then remains on the playable board and can be steered normally.

The ball must not pass through, tunnel through, climb over, become stuck inside, or leave the playable maze through a wall during ordinary input; a meaningful-speed impact must not simply dead-stop without a visible bounce/rebound.
Contact produces a visible block and bounce/rebound; a near-zero-speed touch may settle or slide.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Repeated wall contacts and bounces/rebounds must not disable later movement or corrupt the fixed layout.
Status is `RUNNING`; the ball has not completed the maze.
The ball overlaps the visible central hole/opening of any trap tile listed by `LAYOUT-02`.
The run immediately leaves ordinary running play and begins one trap-recovery transaction.
The same opening contact is counted once.

Trap-rim or surrounding safe-floor contact must not trigger the failure response; a trap opening must not complete the maze, move a trap, regenerate the maze, create multiple counts from one uninterrupted contact, or allow continued player control during recovery.
Status changes to the exact text `TRAP HIT`.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Contact with non-trap floor or the safe outer rim of a trap tile must not trigger this requirement.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: A new opening contact after recovery may trigger it again.
`HAZARD-01` has begun.
Natural recovery sequence.
`TRAP HIT` remains visible for at least 0.75 seconds and no longer than 2.0 seconds.
The displayed trap-hit count increases by exactly one.
By the end of the interval, the ball is restored to the center of `(0,0)` with zero linear and angular velocity, status returns to `RUNNING`, and normal input is enabled.
The ball must not respawn on a trap opening, preserve pre-hit velocity, change the fixed layout, reset the trap-hit count, or accept movement before recovery ends.
The failure text and updated count are readable, followed by the restored running view.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Repeated opening contacts repeat the same transaction. `R` during recovery performs `RESTART-01` and cancels the pending recovery without a later stale reset.
Status is `RUNNING`; the ball has not entered trap recovery.
The ball touches or enters the exit cell `(9,9)`.
The run completes exactly once.
Completion must not occur from entering another cell, pressing an unrelated key, touching a trap, starting the game, or using a hidden shortcut.
Status changes to the exact text `MAZE COMPLETE`.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Further overlap with the exit during the same completed run has no additional effect.
`GOAL-01` has completed the run.
Natural post-completion state and attempted movement input.
The ball is held in a stable completed state, movement input no longer changes its position, the trap-hit count remains readable, and `MAZE COMPLETE` remains visible until `R` or process exit.
Traps, old momentum, timers, or movement input must not change gameplay state after completion.
A new maze must not be generated.
The fixed maze, ball, and persistent completion text remain visible.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: `R` performs `RESTART-01`; `Esc` performs `EXIT-01`.
The playable scene is visible.
Natural state changes.
A readable HUD always shows `STATUS: RUNNING`, `STATUS: TRAP HIT`, or `STATUS: MAZE COMPLETE` according to the true state, plus `TRAP HITS: <non-negative integer>` and `R - RESTART`.
Updates are visible in the same frame or the next rendered frame after the authoritative state change.
HUD text must not contradict the real state, remain hidden, use placeholder text, or show completion before `GOAL-01`.
The exact labels and current values are visible without opening a menu.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Restart and reopen show `STATUS: RUNNING` and `TRAP HITS: 0`.
The game is running, recovering from a trap, or completed.
Press `R` once.
A new clean run begins within 2.0 seconds on the same fixed layout.
The ball is centered at `(0,0)` with zero linear and angular velocity, status is `RUNNING`, trap hits are `0`, input is enabled, and no old recovery or completion action fires later.
Restart must not generate a different layout, preserve trap hits, preserve terminal status, preserve velocity, or require process relaunch.
The restored start state and reset HUD are visible.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Repeated `R` presses leave one healthy current run and do not accumulate duplicate balls, traps, exits, cameras, HUDs, timers, or input bindings.
The process has previously been played in any state and then closed.
Start a genuinely new game process.
The new process begins a fresh run using the same fixed layout, with the ball at `(0,0)`, status `RUNNING`, trap hits `0`, and normal input enabled.
Gameplay progress, completion, trap-hit count, velocity, or pending recovery from the old process must not persist.
The standard initial running view is visible.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: No gameplay save is required or allowed by this task.
Any normal visible game state is active.
Press `Esc` once.
The game requests a normal quit and closes without requiring a debug console, editor stop button, or forced process kill.
`Esc` must not restart, complete, or corrupt the run before exit.
The game window closes normally.

requirements.field: Failure, repetition, restart, reopen, or other boundary
requirements.obligation: Applies during running, trap recovery, and completion.
The project starts, runs, exits, and starts again according to the public instructions.
The main flow uses normal player input and does not depend on an answer button, cheat entry, or direct gameplay-result shortcut.
Critical entries, text, and controls are visible, discoverable, readable, and operable.
Player actions produce perceivable feedback, and visible feedback agrees with the real game state.
No severe error blocks the main flow.
Repeated runs from the same initial conditions are substantially stable.

qualification_test_scope: Distribution, evidence conversion and attribution invariants only; not gameplay semantic qualification.
